entries.name: RigidBody.coordinate_system
entries.docstring:
One can describe the motion of rigid body with a fixed (inertial) coordinate system (X,Y,Z)
    and a moving system (x₁,x₂,x₃) rigidly attached to the body.
entries.snippet:
informal_definition coordinate_system where
  tag := "LL31.3"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.rigid_body_dof
entries.docstring:
A rigid body in three-dimensional space has six degrees of freedom:
    three translational (for the position of its centre of mass) and three
    rotational (for its orientation).
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma rigid_body_dof where
  tag := "LL32-6DF"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.velocity_decomposition
entries.docstring:
The velocity v of any point in a rigid body is
    v = V + Ω × r,
    where V is the velocity of the origin of the moving system and Ω is the angular velocity.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma velocity_decomposition where
  tag := "LL31.L3"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.angular_velocity_is_well_defined
entries.docstring:
The angular velocity of rotation of a rigid body from a system of coordinates fixed in the
    body is independent of the system chosen.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma angular_velocity_is_well_defined where
  tag := "LL32-AM"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.decomposition_of_motion
entries.docstring:
The motion of a rigid body can be decomposed into a translation of some reference point plus a
    rotation about that point. There exists a time-dependent vector V(t) and angular velocity ω(t)
    such that v(r) = V + ω × r, where r is measured from the reference point.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma decomposition_of_motion where
  tag := "LL32-DM"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.center_of_mass_point_moves_as_particle
entries.docstring:
The centre of mass of a rigid body moves as if all mass were concentrated at that
    point and acted upon by the resultant external force: M a_CM = ∑ F_ext.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma center_of_mass_point_moves_as_particle where
  tag := "LL32-CM"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.angular_momentum_about_point
entries.docstring:
The total angular momentum about a point O is L = ∫ r × v dm. With v = V + ω × r about the
    centre of mass, L = R × (M V) + I_CM ω, where R is the centre of mass position.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma angular_momentum_about_point where
  tag := "LL32-L"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.translational_equation_inertial
entries.docstring:
In the inertial frame, the translational equation of motion of a rigid body is given by
    dP/dt = F, where `P` is the total linear momentum and `F` is the total external force acting
    on the body.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma translational_equation_inertial where
  tag := "LL32-TR"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.rotational_equation_inertial
entries.docstring:
In the inertial frame, the rotational equation of motion of a rigid body about the center of
    mass is given by dM/dt = K, where `M` is the total angular momentum and `K` is the total
    external torque.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma rotational_equation_inertial where
  tag := "LL32-ROT"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.kinetic_energy_decomposition
entries.docstring:
The kinetic energy decomposes into translational and rotational parts:
    T = (1/2) M |V|² + (1/2) ω ⋅ I_CM ω.
    Here V is the velocity of the centre of mass and I_CM is the inertia tensor about that point.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma kinetic_energy_decomposition where
  tag := "LL32-TK"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.parallel_axis_theorem
entries.docstring:
If I_O is the inertia tensor about a point O, then the inertia tensor about a parallel point O'
    displaced by a is I_{O'} = I_O + M(|a|² 1 − a ⊗ a). This is the parallel-axis theorem.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma parallel_axis_theorem where
  tag := "LL32-PA"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.principal_axes_of_inertia
entries.docstring:
Because the inertia tensor is real symmetric, there exists an orthonormal basis of principal
    axes in which it is diagonal. The corresponding directions are the principal axes of inertia.
entries.snippet:
informal_definition principal_axes_of_inertia where
  tag := "LL32-PAE"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.principal_axes_of_inertia_bound
entries.docstring: None of the principal moments of inertia can exceed the sum of other two.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma principal_axes_of_inertia_bound where
  tag := "LL32-PAEB"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.asymmetrical_top
entries.docstring: An asymmetrical top is when none of the principal moments of inertia are equal.
entries.snippet:
informal_definition asymmetrical_top where
  tag := "LL32-AST"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.symmetrical_top
entries.docstring: A symmetrical top is when only two of the principal moments of inertia are equal.
entries.snippet:
informal_definition symmetrical_top where
  tag := "LL32-ST"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.spherical_top
entries.docstring: A spherical top is when all three of the principal moments of inertia are equal.
entries.snippet:
informal_definition spherical_top where
  tag := "LL32-SPT"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.RotatingFrame
entries.docstring:
A rotating body-fixed frame is a coordinate system attached to the body
    that rotates with the body relative to an inertial (fixed) frame. The frame
    is characterised by its angular velocity vector Ω(t).
entries.snippet:
informal_definition RotatingFrame where
  tag := "LL32-RF"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.rotating_frame_derivative
entries.docstring:
The time derivative in the rotating frame, d'/dt, is the derivative
    of the components of a vector with respect to time when expressed in the
    rotating (body-fixed) frame.
entries.snippet:
informal_definition rotating_frame_derivative where
  tag := "LL32-dprime"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.transport_law_inertial_rotating
entries.docstring:
For any vector field A(t), its inertial-frame time derivative equals the rotating-frame
    derivative plus the contribution from the frame rotation:
      (dA/dt)_inertial = (dA/dt)_rotating + Ω × A.
    Here Ω is the angular velocity of the rotating frame.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma transport_law_inertial_rotating where
  tag := "LL36-Ltransport"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.transport_law_for_momentum
entries.docstring:
For linear momentum, the relation between inertial and rotating derivatives is
      (dP/dt)_inertial = d'P/dt + Ω × P.
    So, d'P/dt + Ω × P = F which is the linear-momentum equation in the rotating frame.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma transport_law_for_momentum where
  tag := "LL32-transportP"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.transport_law_for_angular_momentum
entries.docstring:
For angular momentum, the relation between inertial and rotating derivatives is
      (dM/dt)_inertial = d'M/dt + Ω × M,
    and with the rotational form of Newton's law M_tot = (dM/dt)_inertial this yields
      d'M/dt + Ω × M = K,
    the angular-momentum equation in the rotating frame.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma transport_law_for_angular_momentum where
  tag := "LL32-transportM"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.euler_equations
entries.docstring:
When motion is described in body-fixed principal axes (I₁, I₂, I₃ diagonal), the equations of
    rotational motion (Euler’s equations) are:
    I₁ dω₁/dt + (I₃ − I₂) ω₂ ω₃ = M₁, with cyclic permutations.
    M is the external torque about the centre of mass.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma euler_equations where
  tag := "LL32-EQ"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.steady_rotation_conditions
entries.docstring:
A rigid body can perform steady (uniform) rotation about any principal axis if the torque about
    that axis vanishes. Stability depends on the ordering of principal moments.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma steady_rotation_conditions where
  tag := "LL32-SR"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.intermediate_axis_instability
entries.docstring:
Rotations about the largest and smallest principal axes are stable under small perturbations;
    rotation about the intermediate axis is unstable (tennis-racket effect).
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma intermediate_axis_instability where
  tag := "LL32-IAI"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.reduction_to_two_body
entries.docstring:
If a rigid body is confined to planar motion, its dynamics reduce to a two-dimensional problem:
    the inertia reduces to a scalar moment and rotation is described
    by a single angular velocity.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma reduction_to_two_body where
  tag := "LL32-RTB"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.rigid_body_work_and_power
entries.docstring:
The power delivered to a rigid body by forces is P = ∑ Fᵢ ⋅ vᵢ = F_tot ⋅ V + M ⋅ ω, where F_tot
    is total force, V the reference point velocity, and M the torque. Translational and rotational
    contributions separate.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma rigid_body_work_and_power where
  tag := "LL32-WP"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: RigidBody.small_oscillations_about_equilibrium
entries.docstring:
Small oscillations about a stable equilibrium orientation are governed by linearised equations
    obtained by expanding energy to second order in angular displacements. Normal modes and
    frequencies depend on inertia and restoring torques.
entries.snippet:
informal_lemma small_oscillations_about_equilibrium where
  tag := "LL32-SO"
  deps := [``RigidBody]

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.FirstOrderFriedmann
entries.docstring:
The first-order Friedmann equation.

- `a : ℝ → ℝ` is the FLRW scale factor as a function of cosmic time `t`.
- `ρ : ℝ → ℝ` is the total energy density as a function of cosmic time `t`.
- `k : ℝ` is the spatial curvature parameter.
- `Λ : ℝ` is the cosmological constant.
- `G : ℝ` is Newton's constant.
- `c : ℝ` is the speed of light. It may be set to 1 for convenience.

Note: We will leave `c` explicit for generality and accounting purposes.

At time `t` the equation reads:
`(a'(t) / a(t))^2 = (8πG/3) ρ(t) − k c^2 / a(t)^2 + Λ c^2 / 3`.
entries.snippet: def FirstOrderFriedmann (a ρ: ℝ → ℝ) (k Λ G c : ℝ) (t : ℝ) : Prop

entries.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.SecondOrderFriedmann
entries.docstring:
The second-order Friedmann equation.
Note: Other sources may call this the Raychaudhuri equation.
We choose not to use that terminology to avoid the Raychaudhuri equation
related to describing congruences of geodesics in general relativity.
- `a : ℝ → ℝ` is the FLRW scale factor as a function of cosmic time `t`.
- `ρ : ℝ → ℝ` is the total energy density as a function of cosmic time `t`.
- `p : ℝ → ℝ` is the pressure. It is related to `ρ` via `p = w * ρ `
- `w` is the equation of state. We will introduce this later.
- `Λ : ℝ` is the cosmological constant.
- `G : ℝ` is Newton's constant.
- `c : ℝ` is the speed of light. It may be set to 1 for convenience.

Note: We will leave `c` explicit for generality and accounting purposes.

At time `t` the equation reads:
`(a''(t) / a (t)) = - (4πG/3) * (ρ(t) + 3 * p(t) / c^2) + Λ * c^2 / 3`.
entries.snippet: def SecondOrderFriedmann (a ρ p: ℝ → ℝ) (Λ G c : ℝ) (t : ℝ) : Prop

  as `- (dₜdₜ a) a / (dₜ a)^2`.

lemma gradLagrangian_one_dimension_electricField (A : ElectromagneticPotentialD 1)

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.canonicalMomentum_eq_gradient_kineticTerm
entries.snippet:
lemma canonicalMomentum_eq_gradient_kineticTerm {d}
    {𝓕 : FreeSpace} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (hA : ContDiff ℝ 2 A) (J : LorentzCurrentDensity d) :
    A.canonicalMomentum 𝓕 J = fun x =>
    gradient (fun (v : Lorentz.Vector d) =>
    kineticTerm 𝓕 (fun x => A x + x (Sum.inl 0) • v) x) 0

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.canonicalMomentum_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma canonicalMomentum_eq {d} {𝓕 : FreeSpace} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (hA : ContDiff ℝ 2 A) (J : LorentzCurrentDensity d) :
    A.canonicalMomentum 𝓕 J = fun x => fun μ =>
      (1/𝓕.μ₀) * η μ μ • A.fieldStrengthMatrix x (μ, Sum.inl 0)

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.canonicalMomentum_eq_electricField
entries.snippet:
lemma canonicalMomentum_eq_electricField {d} {𝓕 : FreeSpace} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (hA : ContDiff ℝ 2 A) (J : LorentzCurrentDensity d) :
    A.canonicalMomentum 𝓕 J = fun x => fun μ =>
      match μ with
      | Sum.inl 0 => 0
      | Sum.inr i => - (1/(𝓕.μ₀ * 𝓕.c)) * A.electricField 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space i

The Hamiltonian associated with an electromagnetic potential
  and a Lorentz current density.

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.hamiltonian_eq_electricField_vectorPotential
entries.snippet:
lemma hamiltonian_eq_electricField_vectorPotential {d} {𝓕 : FreeSpace}
    (A : ElectromagneticPotential d) (hA : ContDiff ℝ 2 A)
    (J : LorentzCurrentDensity d) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    A.hamiltonian 𝓕 J x =
      - (1/ 𝓕.c.val^2 * 𝓕.μ₀⁻¹) * ∑ i, A.electricField 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space i *
      (∂ₜ (A.vectorPotential 𝓕.c · x.space) (x.time 𝓕.c) i) - lagrangian 𝓕 A J x

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.hamiltonian_eq_electricField_scalarPotential
entries.snippet:
lemma hamiltonian_eq_electricField_scalarPotential {d} {𝓕 : FreeSpace}
    (A : ElectromagneticPotential d) (hA : ContDiff ℝ 2 A)
    (J : LorentzCurrentDensity d) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    A.hamiltonian 𝓕 J x =
      (1/ 𝓕.c.val^2 * 𝓕.μ₀⁻¹) * (‖A.electricField 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space‖ ^ 2
      + ⟪A.electricField 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space,
        Space.grad (A.scalarPotential 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) ·) x.space⟫_ℝ)
        - lagrangian 𝓕 A J x

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.hamiltonian_eq_electricField_magneticField
entries.snippet:
lemma hamiltonian_eq_electricField_magneticField (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (hA : ContDiff ℝ 2 A) (J : LorentzCurrentDensity d) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    A.hamiltonian 𝓕 J x = 1/2 * 𝓕.ε₀ * (‖A.electricField 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space‖ ^ 2
      + 𝓕.c ^ 2 / 2 * ∑ i, ∑ j, ‖A.magneticFieldMatrix 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space (i, j)‖ ^ 2)
      + 𝓕.ε₀ * ⟪A.electricField 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space,
        Space.grad (A.scalarPotential 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) ·) x.space⟫_ℝ
      + A.scalarPotential 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space * J.chargeDensity 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space
      - ∑ i, A.vectorPotential 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space i *
        J.currentDensity 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space i

entries.snippet:
lemma isExtrema_iff_gradLagrangian {𝓕 : FreeSpace} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)

    IsExtrema 𝓕 A J ↔ A.gradLagrangian 𝓕 J = 0

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.isExtrema_iff_fieldStrengthMatrix
entries.snippet:
lemma isExtrema_iff_fieldStrengthMatrix {𝓕 : FreeSpace}
    (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (hA : ContDiff ℝ ∞ A) (J : LorentzCurrentDensity d) (hJ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ J) :
    IsExtrema 𝓕 A J ↔
    ∀ x, ∀ ν, ∑ μ, ∂_ μ (A.fieldStrengthMatrix · (μ, ν)) x = 𝓕.μ₀ * J x ν

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.isExtrema_iff_gauss_ampere_magneticFieldMatrix
entries.snippet:
lemma isExtrema_iff_gauss_ampere_magneticFieldMatrix {d} {𝓕 : FreeSpace}
    {A : ElectromagneticPotential d}
    (hA : ContDiff ℝ ∞ A) (J : LorentzCurrentDensity d)
    (hJ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ J) :
    IsExtrema 𝓕 A J ↔ ∀ t, ∀ x, (∇ ⬝ (A.electricField 𝓕.c t)) x = J.chargeDensity 𝓕.c t x / 𝓕.ε₀
    ∧ ∀ i, 𝓕.μ₀ * 𝓕.ε₀ * ∂ₜ (fun t => A.electricField 𝓕.c t x) t i =
    ∑ j, ∂[j] (A.magneticFieldMatrix 𝓕.c t · (j, i)) x - 𝓕.μ₀ * J.currentDensity 𝓕.c t x i

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.time_deriv_electricField_of_isExtrema
entries.snippet:
lemma time_deriv_electricField_of_isExtrema {A : ElectromagneticPotential d}
    {𝓕 : FreeSpace}
    (hA : ContDiff ℝ ∞ A) (J : LorentzCurrentDensity d) (hJ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ J)
    (h : IsExtrema 𝓕 A J) (t : Time) (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    ∂ₜ (A.electricField 𝓕.c · x) t i =
      1 / (𝓕.μ₀ * 𝓕.ε₀) * ∑ j, ∂[j] (A.magneticFieldMatrix 𝓕.c t · (j, i)) x -
      (1/ 𝓕.ε₀) * J.currentDensity 𝓕.c t x i

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.time_deriv_time_deriv_magneticFieldMatrix_of_isExtrema
entries.snippet:
lemma time_deriv_time_deriv_magneticFieldMatrix_of_isExtrema {A : ElectromagneticPotential d}
    {𝓕 : FreeSpace}
    (hA : ContDiff ℝ ∞ A) (J : LorentzCurrentDensity d) (hJd : Differentiable ℝ J)
    (hJ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ J) (h : IsExtrema 𝓕 A J)
    (t : Time) (x : Space d) (i j : Fin d) :
    ∂ₜ (∂ₜ (A.magneticFieldMatrix 𝓕.c · x (i, j))) t =
    𝓕.c ^ 2 * ∑ k, ∂[k] (∂[k] (A.magneticFieldMatrix 𝓕.c t · (i, j))) x +
    𝓕.ε₀⁻¹ * (∂[j] (J.currentDensity 𝓕.c t · i) x - ∂[i] (J.currentDensity 𝓕.c t · j) x)

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.time_deriv_time_deriv_electricField_of_isExtrema
entries.snippet:
lemma time_deriv_time_deriv_electricField_of_isExtrema {A : ElectromagneticPotential d}
    {𝓕 : FreeSpace}
    (hA : ContDiff ℝ ∞ A) (J : LorentzCurrentDensity d)
    (hJ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ J) (h : IsExtrema 𝓕 A J)
    (t : Time) (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    ∂ₜ (∂ₜ (A.electricField 𝓕.c · x i)) t =
      𝓕.c ^ 2 * ∑ j, (∂[j] (∂[j] (A.electricField 𝓕.c t · i)) x) -
      𝓕.c ^ 2 / 𝓕.ε₀ * ∂[i] (J.chargeDensity 𝓕.c t ·) x -
      𝓕.c ^ 2 * 𝓕.μ₀ * ∂ₜ (J.currentDensity 𝓕.c · x i) t

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.kineticTerm_eq_sum_fieldStrengthMatrix

lemma kineticTerm_eq_sum_fieldStrengthMatrix {d} {𝓕 : FreeSpace}

    - 1/(4 * 𝓕.μ₀) * ∑ μ, ∑ ν, ∑ μ', ∑ ν', η μ μ' * η ν ν' *

entries.snippet:
lemma kineticTerm_add_time_mul_const {d} {𝓕 : FreeSpace} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)

    (c : Lorentz.Vector d) (x : SpaceTime d) :

        2 * c ν * (∂_ ν A x (Sum.inl 0)))) + 1/(2 * 𝓕.μ₀) * c (Sum.inl 0) ^2)

    - ∑ i, A.vectorPotential 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space i *

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.lagrangian_eq_electric_magnetic
entries.docstring: The Lagrangian is equal to `1/2 * (ε₀ E^2 - 1/μ₀ B^2) - φρ + A · j`
entries.snippet:
lemma lagrangian_eq_electric_magnetic {d} {𝓕 : FreeSpace}
    (A : ElectromagneticPotential d) (hA : ContDiff ℝ 2 A)
    (J : LorentzCurrentDensity d) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    A.lagrangian 𝓕 J x = 1 / 2 * (𝓕.ε₀ * ‖A.electricField 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space‖ ^ 2 -
    (1 / (2 * 𝓕.μ₀)) * ∑ i, ∑ j, ‖A.magneticFieldMatrix 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space (i, j)‖ ^ 2)
    - A.scalarPotential 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space * J.chargeDensity 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space
    + ∑ i, A.vectorPotential 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space i *
        J.currentDensity 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space i

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.gradLagrangian_eq_electricField_magneticField
entries.snippet:
lemma gradLagrangian_eq_electricField_magneticField {𝓕 : FreeSpace} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d)
    (hA : ContDiff ℝ ∞ A) (J : LorentzCurrentDensity d)
    (hJ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ J) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    A.gradLagrangian 𝓕 J x = (1 / (𝓕.μ₀ * 𝓕.c.val) *
        Space.div (electricField 𝓕.c A ((time 𝓕.c) x)) (space x) +
        - 𝓕.c * J.chargeDensity 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space) •
      Lorentz.Vector.basis (Sum.inl 0) +
    ∑ i, (𝓕.μ₀⁻¹ * (𝓕.ε₀ * 𝓕.μ₀ * ∂ₜ (electricField 𝓕.c A · x.space) ((time 𝓕.c) x) i -
      ∑ j, ∂[j] (magneticFieldMatrix 𝓕.c A (x.time 𝓕.c) · (j, i)) x.space) +
      J.currentDensity 𝓕.c (x.time 𝓕.c) x.space i) •
        Lorentz.Vector.basis (Sum.inr i)

lemma time_integral_mul_pow_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le {d : ℕ} (n m : ℕ) :
    ∃ rt, ∀ (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d.succ, ℝ)),∀ (x : Space d.succ),
    Integrable (fun x : Time => ‖((1 + ‖x‖) ^ rt)⁻¹‖) volume ∧
    ‖x‖ ^ m * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun x => ∫ (t : Time), η (t, x)) x‖ ≤

entries.name: FTheory.SU5.TenQuanta.decompose
entries.docstring:
The decomposition of a `TenQuanta` into a `TenQuanta` which has the
  same `reduce` by has fluxes `{⟨1, 0⟩, ⟨1, 0⟩, ⟨1, 0⟩}` or `{⟨1, 1⟩, ⟨1, -1⟩, ⟨1, 0⟩}` only.

entries.name: FTheory.SU5.TenQuanta.liftCharge
entries.docstring:
Given a finite set of charges `c` the `TenQuanta`
  which do not have exotics, duplicate charges or zero fluxes, which map down to `c`.
  This is defined to be as efficient as possible.

entries.name: FTheory.SU5.TenQuanta.exists_toCharges_toFluxesTen_of_mem_liftCharge
entries.snippet:
lemma exists_toCharges_toFluxesTen_of_mem_liftCharge (c : Finset 𝓩)
    {x : TenQuanta 𝓩} (h : x ∈ liftCharge c) :
    ∃ a : TenQuanta 𝓩, a.reduce = x ∧ a.toCharges.toFinset = c ∧
    (a.toFluxesTen = {⟨1, 0⟩, ⟨1, 0⟩, ⟨1, 0⟩}
    ∨ a.toFluxesTen = {⟨1, 1⟩, ⟨1, -1⟩, ⟨1, 0⟩})

    (h1 : x.toFluxesTen.NoExotics) (h2 : x.toFluxesTen.HasNoZero)

entries.name: FTheory.SU5.TenQuanta.mem_liftCharge_iff
entries.snippet:
lemma mem_liftCharge_iff (c : Finset 𝓩) (x : TenQuanta 𝓩) :
    x ∈ liftCharge c ↔ x.toFluxesTen ∈ FluxesTen.elemsNoExotics
      ∧ x.toCharges.toFinset = c ∧ x.toCharges.Nodup

entries.name: FTheory.SU5.TenQuanta.map_liftCharge

lemma map_liftCharge {𝓩 𝓩1 : Type}[DecidableEq 𝓩] [DecidableEq 𝓩1] [CommRing 𝓩] [CommRing 𝓩1]
    (f : 𝓩 →+* 𝓩1) (c : Finset 𝓩) (F : TenQuanta 𝓩) (h : F ∈ liftCharge c) :
    TenQuanta.reduce (F.map fun y => (f y.1, y.2)) ∈ liftCharge (c.image f)

entries.name: FTheory.SU5.TenQuanta.anomalyCoefficient
entries.docstring:
The anomaly coefficient of a `TenQuanta` is given by the pair of integers:
  `(∑ᵢ qᵢ Nᵢ, 3 * ∑ᵢ qᵢ² Nᵢ)`.

  The first components is for the mixed U(1)-MSSM, see equation (22) of arXiv:1401.5084.
  The second component is for the mixed U(1)Y-U(1)-U(1) gauge anomaly,
    see equation (23) of arXiv:1401.5084.
entries.snippet: def anomalyCoefficient (F : TenQuanta 𝓩) : 𝓩 × 𝓩

entries.name: FTheory.SU5.TenQuanta.anomalyCoefficient_of_map
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma anomalyCoefficient_of_map {𝓩 𝓩1 : Type} [CommRing 𝓩] [CommRing 𝓩1]
    (f : 𝓩 →+* 𝓩1) (F : TenQuanta 𝓩) :
    TenQuanta.anomalyCoefficient (F.map fun y => (f y.1, y.2) : TenQuanta 𝓩1) =
    (f.prodMap f) F.anomalyCoefficient

entries.name: FTheory.SU5.TenQuanta.anomalyCoefficient_of_reduce
entries.snippet:
lemma anomalyCoefficient_of_reduce [DecidableEq 𝓩] (F : TenQuanta 𝓩) :
    F.reduce.anomalyCoefficient = F.anomalyCoefficient

entries.name: Temperature.chain_rule_T_beta
entries.docstring: Chain rule for β(T) : d/dT F(β(T)) = F'(β(T)) * (-1 / (kB * T^2)), within `Ioi 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma chain_rule_T_beta {F : ℝ → ℝ} {F' : ℝ}
    (T : Temperature) (hT_pos : 0 < T.val)
    (hF_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt F F' (Set.Ioi 0) (T.β : ℝ)) :
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun t : ℝ => F (betaFromReal t))
      (F' * (-1 / (kB * (T.val : ℝ)^2))) (Set.Ioi 0) (T.val : ℝ)
